front: What is the molar gas volume at r.t.p.?

back: Room temperature and pressure: about 20 °C and one atmosphere.

front: Amount of a gas from its volume at r.t.p.
How many cm³ are in 1 dm³?
Why does one mole of every gas occupy the same volume?
back: Gas particles are very far apart compared with their size, so the volume depends only on the number of particles.

front: Does the molar gas volume apply to water at r.t.p.?
back: No. Water is a liquid at r.t.p.; 24 dm³ per mole applies only to gases.

front: In a reaction between gases, what do the coefficients give?
back: The ratio of their volumes (at the same temperature and pressure), e.g. $\ce{2CO + O2 -> 2CO2}$: $2 : 1 : 2$ by volume.

front: How do you find the volume of a gas from its mass?
back: amount $=$ mass $\div$ molar mass, then volume $=$ amount $\times 24\ \text{dm}^3$.

front: What volume does 1 mol of $\ce{O2}$ occupy at r.t.p.?
back: $24\ \text{dm}^3$, the same as 1 mol of any gas (count moles of molecules).

front: What is the most common error in gas-volume calculations?
back: Dividing a volume in cm³ by 24 instead of 24 000 (or forgetting to convert cm³ to dm³).
